info.bio: Living Colour comenzó como un trío compuesto por Vernon Reid (guitarra), Muzz Skillings (bajo) y Will Calhoun (batería). Corey Glover (voz) fue integrado a la banda después de que Vernon Reid lo escucho cantar el "Feliz Cumpleaños" en la casa de un amigo. El grupo se presentó durante varios años en clubs y salas de Estados Unidos, haciendo habitual sus shows en el CBGB neoyorquino, previo a su primer disco. Vernon Reid era el único que contaba con experiencia musical

scenes.name: Black rock
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: «El funk es blues acelerado» (Clinton). Pese a Chuck Berry, Little Richard o Bo Diddley, el rock se volvió una forma blanca y la invasión británica reforzó el mito, aunque sus grupos venían del blues negro. Hendrix y Sly lo desmontaron a finales de los sesenta, pero la industria resegregó el rock en pocos años, hasta Prince. El blues eléctrico (Muddy Waters, con su «gran caída tras el golpe del tambor») tuvo su revival ante el público blanco. En la Costa Oeste, multirracial y lejos de los problemas del Norte y del Sur, florecieron bandas mestizas (Sly, Tower of Power, Santana): la influencia del rock psicodélico convirtió el funk de un R&B salvaje en algo universal. A mediados de los setenta el black rock se convirtió en funk, porque la radio obligó a quitar los solos de guitarra; solo algunos resistieron («Who Says a Funk Band Can’t Play Rock?!» de Funkadelic, Slave, Mother’s Finest, los Isley) hasta Prince y la Black Rock Coalition de Vernon Reid (1985), y en los noventa Living Colour, Body Count, Bad Brains o Fishbone.

scenes.name: Funk rock: Chili Peppers, Primus y la Black Rock Coalition
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: A los blancos les era mucho más fácil tocar funk y grabar: Jane’s Addiction debutó con un directo, Primus de Les Claypool (devoto de Larry Graham), los Limbomaniacs con Bootsy y Maceo, Praxis. Los Red Hot Chili Peppers de Anthony Kiedis y Flea, con Freaky Styley producido por Clinton (1985), versionaron a Sly, los Meters y Stevie y llevaron a P-Funk al escenario de los Grammy de 1993; pero los creadores del funk rock, como los P-Funk All Stars, no tenían esa libertad. En Nueva York Living Colour de Vernon Reid no conseguía contrato pese a tener a Mick Jagger de fan, y Reid y Greg Tate fundaron en 1985 la Black Rock Coalition: «El rock and roll es música negra y nosotros somos sus herederos», contra el «rock de orientación apartheid». Abrió paso a Steve Coleman, Me’Shell NdegéOcello, James Blood Ulmer o el Kelvynator de Kelvyn Bell.

scenes.name: Funk metal, arte y autoparodia
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A principios de los noventa el metal empieza a perder definición en su periferia: el lite metal se acerca al pop con secciones de cuerda (Damn Yankees), otros grupos meten el funk heredado de las mezclas de punk y funk (Living Colour, Faith No More) cortando el poder del metal con ironía, Jane’s Addiction añade art rock reflexivo y Scatterbrain juega con el género de forma consciente, socavando su autenticidad. Weinstein lo ve como el proceso normal de cambio cultural de un género que conserva su núcleo.
scenes.family: Cruces: rap, funk, industrial, grunge y nu metal

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Lineup
podcast.body: Living Colour was part of the lineup for the first Lollapalooza festival in the summer of 1991.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
podcast.body: Living Colour performed at the inaugural Lollapalooza tour in the summer of 1991, which proved that a large audience was willing to pay to see a lineup of decidedly non-mainstream bands. "Along with founding band Jane's addiction, the line up included Suzy and the band sheets, living color, iced tea and body count, butthole surfers, Rawens band and some weirdo group that was never going to go anywhere called Nine-inch Nails."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Performance at First Lollapalooza (1991)
podcast.body: Living Color was featured on the bill of the first-ever Lollapalooza tour in 1991, cementing their status in the alternative music scene. "ended up on the first ever La La Palusatour in 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: All-Black Funk Metal Band
podcast.body: Living Color emerged as an all-black funk metal band around the time Fishbone was peaking, fusing funk and metal in their sound. "along came Living Color, an All Black Funk Metal Band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breaking Racial Barriers in Rock
podcast.body: Living Colour, composed of four black guys from New York, was a "revelation" in the mid-1980s, playing heavy hard rock in a rock scene that was largely segregated. Their presence challenged the racial divide, especially as regular performers at the famous punk club CBGB. "Four black guys from New York playing heavy, hard rock."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Corey Glover's Acting Role
podcast.body: Singer Corey Glover also pursued an acting career, notably appearing as Private Francis in Oliver Stone's 1986 film "Platoon." "The singer is Corey Glover, an actor who can be seen playing private frances in the 1986 Oliver Stone movie Platoon."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Diverse Influences
podcast.body: The band drew inspiration from a wide range of artists including James Brown, Funkadelic, Run DMC, Sly and the Family Stone, Led Zeppelin, Van Halen, and The Clash. "They were inspired equally by James Brown, Funkadelic, Run DMC, Slion the Family Stone, and Led Zeppelin Van Halen, and the Clash."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early New York City Performances
podcast.body: Living Color established a reputation for their skilled musicianship and hard-rocking ability by playing extensively around New York City, including at venues like CBGB. "They started playing around New York City, including CBGB, and quickly established a reputation from being great players with an ability to rock really, really hard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Groundbreaking Funk Metal Sound
podcast.body: Living Colour, a band of four Black men from New York City, created a funk metal sound that laid the groundwork for many groups of the 1990s. Their influence was felt across bands like Rage Against the Machine, 311, Primus, and even Korn. "The resulting funk metal laid the groundwork for many groups of the 1990s, ranging from rage against the machine to 311 to primus to even corn."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Nu-Metal Bands
podcast.body: Living Color's fusion of funk and metal proved influential, inspiring groups like Rage Against the Machine and Limp Bizkit. "another band that inspired groups like Rage Against the Machine, and Limbiscuit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: MTV and Grammy Success
podcast.body: The band achieved considerable success, becoming "MTV heroes and ended up winning a bunch of Grammy Awards," showcasing the widespread appeal of their genre-bending music. "Living color became MTV heroes and ended up winning a bunch of Grammy Awards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reaching White Audiences
podcast.body: Living Color was mentioned as one of the groups that helped rap and hip hop reach more white kids, contributing to the genre's expanding appeal. "And thanks to groups like Body Count, Living Color, the Beastie Boys and Rage Against the Machine, rap and hip hop was able to reach both more white kids."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tours with Major Rock Acts
podcast.body: Following the success of their debut, they toured with high-profile bands such as Guns N' Roses and The Rolling Stones. "They toured with guns and roses and the rolling stones."
